note: endpoint contract design contract design reviewed 2026-09-11; network location, geocoder and attestation contracts added 2026-09-26, with the owner's network location and geocoder choices recorded the same day. Source observations and project server policy are distinct. No signup, deployment, native test or release acceptance is implied. Blockers gate the named implementation task; validation proves document consistency only.

Independent Git bundles with branch/tag verification and tested restoration; no publishing authority

topology.eu_primary: Project HTTP/TCP delivery uses the selected German primary with TLS on own servers and no CDN. INWX authoritative DNS is separately administered and uses global Anycast; the chosen recursive DNS default and upstream acquisition jurisdictions are disclosed separately.
topology.non_eu_mirror: Independent 1984 Iceland candidate serves identical verified release objects, proof bundles and recovery/site copy. Separate provider account and SSH identities; no private signing keys. Canonical selector publication and mirror freshness are checked separately; a first installer still needs an independently obtained verification root.
topology.community_separation: Community/federation hosts and credentials are separate from release/update infrastructure . A community-host compromise cannot administer release infrastructure: distinct hosts, distinct credentials, no shared admin path, no release secrets on community hosts.
topology.management_path: Owner workstation -> distinct host-scoped SSH identities over protected management VPN; provider console is an independent recovery path. Community accounts, federation login, git tokens and serving processes cannot use either path. infrastructure staging proves denied access and recovery; no addresses or secret values in public configuration.

client_defaults.name: private-dns
client_defaults.disclosure: Swiss operator; the device connects directly to its chosen resolver. INWX authoritative DNS is a separate layer. dns0.eu is not selected: availability was not established during this review. Publish active resolver and supported alternatives; do not silently fall back to plaintext.

client_defaults.name: authenticated-time
client_defaults.default: Server-side NTS source agreement; Netnod is a verified EU service candidate, PTB authenticated support remains unverified.
client_defaults.disclosure: Netnod is Swedish. Multiple Netnod hosts are one operator, not independent operators. Six source slots and at least three agreeing samples are project service policy, not fields or quorum checks in the Android HTTPS client. Qualify source diversity in TIME-SOURCES before enabling this service.

client_defaults.name: network-location
client_defaults.default: Off. Opt-in choices: the DiamaneOS EU relay to Apple's location service (location.diamaneos.de), Apple's service directly (gs-loc.apple.com) or Apple's China service directly (gs-loc-cn.apple.com). Owner decision 2026-09-26, the same choices as GrapheneOS with its proxy replaced by the DiamaneOS relay.
client_defaults.disclosure: Apple is a US operator; the China choice goes to Apple's separate service for China (gs-loc-cn.apple.com), whose operator and data location were not checked. Every choice sends nearby Wi-Fi access points and cells, which reveal approximate location, to Apple. The EU relay keeps no cache and no per-request logs and hides the device IP from Apple; the direct choices also give Apple the device IP. The setup wizard's location switch must not turn any of them on silently. The network position seeds the GNSS engine: in an indoor owner test on the FP6 (2026-09-26), GPS alone gave no fix within several minutes; with Apple directly the first network fix arrived about 35 s after the app's request and GPS locked about 1 s later.

client_defaults.name: geocoder
client_defaults.default: Off. DiamaneOS hosts no geocoder for now (owner decision 2026-09-26); users may opt in to OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) directly, with a DiamaneOS User-Agent.
client_defaults.disclosure: Run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation, registered in England and Wales (UK). When the user opts in, OpenStreetMap sees the device IP, the searched text or the queried coordinates (usually the user's own location), the language and the User-Agent; no DiamaneOS server is in the path. Use stays within OpenStreetMap's Nominatim usage policy (identify the app, low request rate, attribution). Ask the OpenStreetMap Foundation before it becomes anything more than an opt-in. Self-hosting can be revisited if people use it.

endpoints.path_method: GET /{DEVICE}-{channel}; GET /{DEVICE}-incremental-{current}-{target}.zip, falling back on 404 to /{DEVICE}-ota_update-{target}.zip; optional Range.
request_fields: Model, channel and current/target incremental in path; Range: bytes={offset}- on resume.
response_fields: Selector first line: targetIncremental targetBuildDate targetDevice targetChannel (space separated); date is Unix seconds.
ZIP byte stream; HTTP 206 on valid Range, 404 missing object; signed OTA metadata checked inside package.
endpoints.verification_root: RecoverySystem.verifyPackage with device-pinned OTA certificates; update_engine payload checks; expected device/channel and newer build date checked. Release key ceremony release key ceremony and verified boot/rollback remain separate. No invented transparency verification in current Updater.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Observed: connect/read 30 s; scheduled checks every 6 h, failed background job rescheduled after >=4 min. Server transfer deadline 3600 s; one attempt per request. No blanket three-retry native claim.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Project selector body <=4096 bytes; canonical selector publication check <=24 h, HTTP max-age=5. Verified immutable objects remain available by exact name within 64 GiB store; never garbage-collect referenced objects. Publish bytes then selector atomically.
endpoints.failure_fallback: No fresh approved selector: HTTP 503 (no redirect); existing installed OS runs. Invalid signature/metadata: client refuses update. Missing incremental: full OTA path. Interrupted bytes remain untrusted until full verification. Offline signed recovery/OTA is owned by offline signed OTA / release publication.
endpoints.exposed_data: IP and requested path are visible to the EU service; no project user account is required. Path reveals OS model/version/channel. Updater does not need a serial in the request.
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

endpoints.purpose: Signed catalog and gzip APK delivery
endpoints.protocol: metadata.1.{KEY_VERSION}.sjson: JSON bytes + LF + 100 base64 signature characters + LF. Signify Ed25519 verification covers original JSON bytes; 304 reuses an already verified repo.
endpoints.path_method: GET /metadata.1.{KEY_VERSION}.sjson with optional If-None-Match; GET /packages/{manifestPackageName}/{versionCode}/{name}.gz with optional Range.
request_fields: Catalog ETag; package/version/name in download path; Range offset. Local installed package filtering is not a transmitted package inventory.
response_fields: JSON time (Unix seconds) and packages; per-variant metadata with packages, hashes, sizes and gzSizes arrays; exact parser in apps-format.
Signed envelope <=8 MiB project cap; APK gzip and decoded size each <=8 GiB and equal signed metadata; SHA-256 decoded APK and installed signer checks.
endpoints.verification_root: Own signify catalog verification key; package APK certificates checked by installer. Mirror acquisition authenticates upstream catalog/cert before project catalog signing. No hash or TLS alone replaces either signature boundary.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Observed: 10 s connect /30 s read. Upstream readBytes has no total catalog cap; implement 8 MiB stream cap in Apps repository integration. Server has bounded streams; clients retain native scheduling until tested.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Client rejects timestamps below max(current repo, 1770000000); no observed wall-clock TTL. Project stops serving current catalog after 24 h without an authoritative freshness check, retains verified objects and verified client cache. 304 only for a verified matching ETag.
endpoints.failure_fallback: Catalog unavailable: HTTP 503; existing verified client cache may still describe/install cached packages under native policy, not claimed automatically age-rejected. endpoints.protocol: HTTPS GET /generate_204; HTTP 204 empty body and X-Time decimal signed-64-bit Unix milliseconds. No client nonce or quorum fields. Client warms connection then requests again with Connection: close; Date fallback exists if X-Time missing/unparseable.
request_fields: No request body; ordinary TLS/HTTP headers.
response_fields: HTTP 204; zero response body bytes; X-Time integer Unix milliseconds; Cache-Control: no-store.
endpoints.verification_root: Inherited bootstrap TLS still checks chain/hostname but treats certificate dates relative to build time; time before Build.TIME is rejected. Do not turn off verification. NTS validation and quorum are server responsibilities.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Observed config_ntpTimeout=5000 ms; first successful configured URL returns. Serve within 5 s total, one request attempt; underlying client warmup makes two GETs. No upstream time lookup per user request.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Never cache time. Serve only when >=3 of 6 authenticated source slots agree within 500 ms and samples <=300 s old (chosen server policy, untested). Check health before every response; freshness based on monotonic sampling age.
endpoints.failure_fallback: No quorum, stale samples, implausible time: HTTP 503 and no X-Time header; do not send 204, cached time or invented agreement. Client may retain its prior estimate and try configured alternatives. time and connectivity integration must prove 503/Date handling and fresh-device TLS bootstrap on native client.
endpoints.exposed_data: IP and requested path are visible to the EU service; no project user account is required. NTS providers receive service IP only; no client query forwarded. The pinned time client uses getPrivateDnsBypassingCopy for bootstrap resolution, so the network resolver may see its hostname even with Quad9 configured; this is distinct from the default DoT data path.
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

implementation_blockers.description: Qualify six NTS source slots and operator independence, serve only with >=3 agreeing fresh samples; Netnod capabilities verified but PTB NTS unverified. Validate 500 ms/300 s health policy and source loss/clock step/old-build TLS behavior before activation. DNS filtering / time and connectivity integration must bind and disclose bootstrap DNS bypass behavior; the current code does not establish all-bootstrap DNS encryption.

endpoints.cache_freshness: No cached probe success; endpoint returns current reachability only. Neither probe is an update/attestation trust service.

Vanadium also probes this host itself (HTTP and HTTPS /generate_204) while the OS setting selects the default servers, and its DNS-over-HTTPS probe asks the user's resolver for this hostname even when the OS setting turns checks off. Repointing Vanadium needs a rebuilt browser (FP6-111).
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

endpoints.consumer: Android Connectivity CertificateTransparencyDownloader (distinct from browser component CT updates)
endpoints.consumer_version: Exact revisions, paths and symbols in source_refs; research-pin app sources are not accepted shipping APK bindings.
endpoints.protocol: Download allowlisted RSA public key then signature and matching list; client independently allowlists key and verifies SHA256withRSA before install.
endpoints.path_method: GET /android/certificate_transparency/log_list.pub; GET /android/certificate_transparency/v2/log_list.json and /v2/log_list.sig; GET /android/certificate_transparency/v3/log_list.ctfb and /v3/log_list.sig (all v2/v3 paths under common prefix).
response_fields: Base64 X.509 RSA public key; base64 signature; v2 JSON list or v3 FlatBuffer list (not interchangeable).
endpoints.verification_root: SignatureVerifier loads R.raw.ct_public_keys independently, rejects downloaded keys outside allowlist and verifies SHA256withRSA over exact content bytes. Preserve that boundary and independently pin keys at staging.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Inherited DownloadManager schedules transfers; downloader readAllBytes lacks this project total bound. Project: 5 s connect, 15 s idle, 60 s total, <=8 MiB per object, hourly scheduler.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Atomically stage each list/signature pair and verified key, keeping prior versions in 64 MiB store. Project stops serving activation set after 48 h without validated refresh; alert after 24 h. Immutable archived bytes are not advertised as current.
endpoints.failure_fallback: Bad signature/key, partial pair or refresh failure: preserve last verified pair only until 48 h then 503. Pinned Conscrypt marks a list non-compliant if its timestamp is in the future or older than 70 days (strictly greater); checkCT skips CT enforcement when the store is non-compliant/unusable. This inherited fail-open behavior is a security degradation, not a total TLS outage and not a new project bypass. Alert on list age and refresh failures; do not rewrite signed timestamps or claim server 503 prevents native fail-open.
endpoints.exposed_data: IP and requested path are visible to the EU service; no project user account is required. Google sees mirror IP and fixed file paths; no device requests forwarded.
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

upstreams.data: Mirror IP and fixed CT paths.

endpoints.consumer: DnsResolver DnsTlsTransport.makeDnsQuery and NetworkMonitor private-DNS checks
endpoints.consumer_version: Exact revisions, paths and symbols in source_refs; research-pin app sources are not accepted shipping APK bindings.
endpoints.purpose: Validate configured Private DNS resolver; DNS records, not another web server
endpoints.protocol: DNS AAAA IN query over chosen resolver/DoT. DnsTlsTransport uses random six-character prefix plus -dnsotls-ds.dnscheck.grapheneos.org. NetworkMonitor also probes under the configured suffix.
endpoints.path_method: DNS query: {random}-dnsotls-ds.dnscheck.diamaneos.de. Authoritative wildcard *.dnscheck.diamaneos.de; no HTTP URL.
request_fields: Random probe label, QTYPE AAAA, QCLASS IN; DNS wire header.
response_fields: Wildcard A 192.0.2.1 and AAAA 100::1, TTL 3600; discard/documentation addresses are answers, not machines to deploy.
endpoints.verification_root: Chosen DoT resolver TLS authentication; native checkDnsResponse checks minimum 12-byte response/header and one question, not strictly a positive AAAA answer. DNS response is not proof of whole internet reachability.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Native resolver scheduling remains independent of web probes. Query/answer staging ceiling 512 bytes; selected service checks 10 s. Authoritative provider rate/latency policy is external, not enforced by our VPS.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Authoritative TTL 3600; recursive caches may keep records. Never mistake cached DNS answers for live connectivity.
endpoints.failure_fallback: Authoritative/resolver outage: DNS failure and native Private DNS validation/backoff; no HTTP fallback service. Preserve explicit standard-resolver setting. Non-answer acceptance in inherited validator is documented, not claimed cryptographic positive-answer proof.
endpoints.exposed_data: Configured recursive resolver sees device IP and query. INWX authority normally sees recursive resolver IP and query; authoritative query metadata may still reveal OS use. Quad9 is a Swiss direct-device default exception, not an EU proxy. INWX uses global Anycast: German operator jurisdiction does not mean all DNS query processing occurs in Germany. The resolver sends this probe name to the user's Private DNS provider even when connectivity checks are turned off, because the probe suffix falls back to the default (branding inventory OP-BRANDING NET-04).
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

upstreams.data: Device IP and DNS queries; user-selected resolver may differ.

example.expected: DNS zone example, not an HTTPS service; wildcard must cover both resolver probe labels and return configured records. DNSSEC/MFA provisioning is infrastructure staging.

endpoints.consumer: NetworkLocation ApplePositioningService (app.grapheneos.networklocation), selected by the network location setting
endpoints.consumer_version: Exact revisions, paths and symbols in source_refs; research-pin app sources are not accepted shipping APK bindings.
endpoints.purpose: Wi-Fi and cell positioning through a DiamaneOS EU relay for Apple's location service, one of three opt-in choices (the others are Apple directly and Apple China directly); network location is off by default
endpoints.protocol: HTTPS POST in Apple's location request format: a short binary header (request version, locale, client identifier and version, request code) followed by a length-prefixed protobuf ALSLocationRequest naming nearby Wi-Fi access points and cells. The response skips a 10-byte header and carries a protobuf ALSLocationResponse. The client sends macOS locationd headers. A proxy forwards the body unchanged and adds no identifiers.
request_fields: Binary header: request version 1, locale, client identifier, client version, request code, protobuf length.
Protobuf ALSLocationRequest: nearby Wi-Fi access point identifiers and/or cell identifiers, plus fixed client metadata.
response_fields: 10 header bytes the client skips, then protobuf ALSLocationResponse with positions for the queried access points or cells; any non-200 status is a failure.
endpoints.verification_root: HTTPS with system trust (the client uses a modern-TLS socket factory). Positions are a location hint, not a trust decision; nothing beyond TLS authenticates them.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Client connect and read timeouts are 10 s each; one request per lookup, with client-side throttling and caches deciding re-requests. The proxy answers within the client deadline with one upstream attempt and no server retries.
endpoints.cache_freshness: No proxy cache: cached queries would keep location history. The client keeps its own time-limited cache.
endpoints.failure_fallback: Proxy or upstream outage: pass an error status through (5xx) and never synthesize positions. The client falls back to satellite positioning or no network location. The inherited setting also offers Apple directly, Apple China and off; DiamaneOS keeps all of them and offers this relay in place of GrapheneOS's proxy, off by default (owner decision 2026-09-26).
endpoints.exposed_data: The EU proxy sees the device IP and the list of nearby Wi-Fi access points and cells, which reveals the user's approximate location. Apple receives the same query with the proxy's IP instead of the device's. If the user chooses Apple directly or Apple China directly instead, Apple (or its service for China) also sees the device IP and no DiamaneOS server is in the path. Network location is off by default, but the inherited setup wizard's location switch turns it on (branding inventory OP-BRANDING NET-13; to confirm on the device); the DiamaneOS setup wizard must not turn it on silently.
endpoints.retention: No access/body/query/header logs. Aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service. Providers and non-project upstreams have their own linked policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

upstreams.data: Nearby Wi-Fi access points and cells in Apple's request format; the proxy IP replaces the device IP.

implementation_blockers.description: Scope decided 2026-09-26 (owner): network location offers the DiamaneOS EU relay, Apple directly and Apple China directly as user choices, off by default, as GrapheneOS does; DiamaneOS hosts no geocoder, and geocoding is off by default with OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim directly as the opt-in (see GEOCODER-HOSTING). FP6-103 owns both. Remaining before activation: the server URLs are literals in the NetworkLocation app (ApplePositioningService.getServerUrl, NominatimGeocoder.getServerBaseUrl), so a NetworkLocation fork repoints the relay, leaves no option that reaches GrapheneOS's servers and sends a DiamaneOS User-Agent to Nominatim (the Apple request keeps its locationd headers); its package ID stays unchanged. Confirm on FP6 what the inherited setup wizard's location switch selects; the SetupWizard2 fork (with FP6-070) must select the chosen service or off and never turn network location on silently. Bind the relay's request/response ceilings from captured native traffic.

example.expected: The owning task supplies captured native request and response fixtures plus malformed, oversized and upstream-outage cases before activation; no synthetic position fixture is claimed.

endpoints.consumer: NetworkLocation NominatimGeocoder (the Android Geocoder provider), selected by the geocoder setting
endpoints.consumer_version: Exact revisions, paths and symbols in source_refs; research-pin app sources are not accepted shipping APK bindings.
endpoints.purpose: Turns place names into coordinates and coordinates into addresses for apps that use Android's Geocoder, only when the user turns geocoding on. DiamaneOS hosts no geocoder for now (owner decision 2026-09-26): the opt-in goes directly to OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim, and geocoder.diamaneos.de is only reserved in case self-hosting is revisited.
endpoints.protocol: HTTPS GET of the Nominatim API with format=geocodejson: /search for place names (optionally bounded to a box) and /reverse for coordinates at zoom 18, with addressdetails and extratags. The client sends Accept-Language from the requested locale and the User-Agent 'GrapheneOS geocoder 1', which a DiamaneOS fork must change.
request_fields: Query text, or latitude and longitude; result limit; optional bounding box; Accept-Language; client User-Agent.
response_fields: GeocodeJSON FeatureCollection with geometry and address fields. The literal body {"error":"Unable to geocode"} means no result; any non-200 status is a failure.
endpoints.verification_root: HTTPS with system trust (modern-TLS socket factory). Results are map data, not a security decision.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Client connect and read timeouts are 10 s each; one request per call. No DiamaneOS server: the geocode limits profile applies only if self-hosting is revisited. OpenStreetMap's usage policy caps an app at 1 request per second across all its users.
endpoints.cache_freshness: No DiamaneOS server, so no DiamaneOS cache of queries or answers, which reveal places a user looks up. Map data freshness is OpenStreetMap's.
endpoints.failure_fallback: OpenStreetMap outage, overload or refusal: an error status, so apps get no result rather than invented addresses. The DiamaneOS setting offers only off (the default) and OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim.
endpoints.exposed_data: When the user opts in, OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim (the OpenStreetMap Foundation, UK) sees the device IP, the searched text or the queried coordinates, the user's language and the client User-Agent; no DiamaneOS server is in the path. Reverse-geocoded coordinates are usually the user's own location. Geocoding is off by default.
endpoints.retention: No DiamaneOS server, so no project logs. Opted-in queries fall under the OpenStreetMap Foundation's own policies; zero project logs does not assert zero upstream retention.

Decided 2026-09-26 (owner): DiamaneOS hosts no geocoder for now. Geocoding stays off by default; users may opt in to OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim directly. Self-hosting can be revisited if people use it. Before enabling the opt-in: the NetworkLocation fork sends a User-Agent that names DiamaneOS, and use stays within OpenStreetMap's Nominatim usage policy: identify the app, keep a low request rate (the policy's absolute maximum is 1 request per second, counted across all users of an app) and show OpenStreetMap attribution for the ODbL data. endpoints.consumer: Auditor RemoteVerifyJob and SubmitSampleJob (app.attestation.auditor, shipped as a prebuilt)
endpoints.consumer_version: Exact revisions, paths and symbols in source_refs; research-pin app sources are not accepted shipping APK bindings.
endpoints.purpose: Optional remote verification of a paired device's hardware-backed attestation, and optional submission of attestation samples
endpoints.protocol: HTTPS POST to /auditor/challenge (get a single-use challenge), /auditor/verify (send the attestation for the paired account) and /auditor/submit (sample submission). Remote verification runs as a periodic job (default every 4 hours; 1 hour to 7 days) after the user pairs the device with an account. Sample submission runs only when the user starts it.
request_fields: verify: identifiers stored when the device was paired, and the serialized attestation for the server challenge.
submit: attestation certificate chains (TEE, and StrongBox where present), the kernel uname string and the full system property list.
response_fields: challenge: challenge bytes; verify: success or failure and any schedule change; submit: status. Exact fields to be bound from the fork and server.
endpoints.verification_root: HTTPS with system trust. The server checks attestation against pinned OS signing keys and supported devices; GrapheneOS's server has neither DiamaneOS keys nor the FP6.
endpoints.timeout_retry: Client connect and read timeouts are 30 s; the job scheduler retries with its own backoff. The server answers each request once, with no server retries.
endpoints.cache_freshness: Never cache challenges or verification results; each challenge is single use.
endpoints.failure_fallback: Outage: the job fails and the app shows a failed remote check; never report success without a verified attestation. Local device-to-device verification in Auditor does not use this service.
endpoints.exposed_data: The service sees account identifiers from pairing, the device IP, and attestation data including OS version and patch level. Sample submission adds the full system property list, attestation certificate chains and the kernel version. Both features are opt-in.
endpoints.retention: The service keeps verification history for paired accounts, which is its purpose; the retention period is set in FP6-106. No access or body logs otherwise; aggregate counters only: 24 hours, 10 MiB cap per service.

implementation_blockers.description: Fork Auditor with DiamaneOS key pins, FP6 support and the DiamaneOS server (the domain is a literal in RemoteVerifyJob); its package ID stays unchanged (owner decision 2026-09-26). Run an attestation server built from source. Until then DiamaneOS builds must not offer remote verification or sample submission against GrapheneOS's server. Set history retention and sample handling before activation. Unlike every other contract this service keeps state (paired accounts, history), so it must not run on the read-only release host; the services model needs a separate host role and credentials for it before activation.

example.expected: The owning task supplies fixtures from the forked client and server, plus replayed-challenge, wrong-key, unsupported-device and outage cases, before activation.
